Decision: split into 12 children. Four reuse comparator-accepted declarations at byte-identical frozen types: abstract_dimension_reduction, dimred_im_mass_measure, dtc_blowUp_scaling and cone_current_imrep_measure_smul_image. Eight are new obligations with fresh idtp_fons_ names. Depth 3 < 6.

1. Correction of attempt 1 (the two required changes).
- Attempt 1's rationale wrongly said that monotonicity (MON), moving_blowups (MB), density_and_tangent_cones (DTC), cone_splitting (CS) and one_dim_cones (ODC) remained available to this node. They were not available, for three reasons.
  - The immutable handoff registers only weak_limit_mass_bound (WLMB) and density_eq_multiplicity_ae (DEM), and ancestor dependencies are not inherited.
  - Runtime._overlay_accepted_children overlays only this node's children and depends_on.
  - All five nodes are unaccepted (dag.json 11:00Z: MON rlcr-lean, MB/DTC/CS/ODC speculative-ready). Runtime._existing_lean_name_problem therefore forbids reusing their names under this parent.
- Attempt 1's assembly was consequently only conditional. That statement is withdrawn.
- This attempt closes the gap in three ways.
  - (a) MB is no longer used at all, by departure [D3] below. WLMB is no longer used either.
  - (b) MON, DTC, CS and ODC become registered obligations with fresh names and frozen types byte-identical to the originals: monotonicity, tangent_cones, cone_splitting and one_dim_cones.
  - (c) The original MON, DTC and CS proofs all invoke minimizing_implies_stationary, which is also unaccepted and unregistered. It becomes the registered obligation stationarity (fresh name, type MinimizingImpliesStationary). The original CS handoff omits this use; here it is registered.
- Each new obligation's natural proof is the original node's parent-supplied proof, accepted in its parent's decomposition audit. It is reproduced with every prerequisite reference re-targeted to a registered sibling, and its numbered argument is unchanged.
- The selected node's own Lean proof now uses only proposed children and its registered dependency DEM. This is checked in item 6.

2. Departure [D3]: the zero-scale class. The supplied step 2 builds Simon's class 𝒯 from weak limits of blow-ups at moving centres. That needs MB, the diagonal lemma, uniform mass bounds (WLMB) and the countable-test criterion (C).
- Appendix A.4 (abstract_dimension_reduction) only needs a family closed under the rescalings of A.1 that contains the tangent limits of A.2.
- The child cone_class therefore takes, as zero-scale members, the weights of ALL minimizing cycles S of ℝ^P (IsMinimizingIn S univ, ∂S = 0).
- Tangent limits are again members.
  - For positive-scale members they are tangent cones of T, from DTC (2) at a support point, or 0.
  - For minimizing cycles they come from DTC (2) with U = N = ℝ^P (ℝ^P is an embedded C² submanifold of itself), or 0.
  - Weak limits of blow-ups of cycles are cycles, so the limits are minimizing cycles.
- Rescalings of minimizing cycles are minimizing cycles (dtc_blowUp_scaling (3), with ∂ commuting with the affine push-forward).
- All other parent arguments are kept: (a)–(c), (f), the density functions (i)–(ix), domain recovery from mass and barycenter, and (T3s). The properties (M1)–(M9) consumed by class_reduction are verified for this class.
- Zero-scale members have total mass 0 or ∞ and the lower bound ω_nρ^n on balls around support points (MON with N = ℝ^P), exactly as Simon's zero-scale members do. So domain recovery (M6), support semicontinuity (M7), (M9) and the planar exclusion (M8) go through unchanged.

4. Assembly of idtp_flat_off_null_set. This is supplied steps 1, 2 (choice of 𝒞) and 5, with β_j := 1/(j + 1) in place of 2^{−j}. Let n, k, ℓ, U, N, T satisfy the hypotheses, P := n + k and dens as in cone_class.
- Choose a countable dense D_set ⊆ ℝ^P and let 𝒞 := {(z, q) ∈ D_set × ℚ : q > 0, closedBall z (2q) ⊆ U, spt T ∩ B_{2q}(z) ≠ ∅}, a countable set.
- For (z, q) ∈ 𝒞, cone_class applies with these discharges: (DEM) by Submission.idtp_imrep_measure_density_ae (registered dependency), (MON) by monotonicity, (DTC) by tangent_cones, and (PS) by planar_support applied to cone_splitting and one_dim_cones.
- For j ∈ ℕ, class_reduction (same 𝓜, D, Λ, dens, μ₀; β_j) gives Z_{z,q,j}: Z = ∅ if n = 1, μH[n − 2 + α](Z) = 0 for α > 0, and β_j-flatness inside B_2(0) of every w ∈ B_1(0) ∩ spt μ₀ ∖ Z. For (z, q) ∉ 𝒞 put Z := ∅.
- Put F := ⋃_{(z,q)∈𝒞} ⋃_j (z + q·Z_{z,q,j}).
- F is null. If n = 1, every Z is empty. If n ≥ 2, then n − 2 + α > 0 and w ↦ z + qw is q-Lipschitz, so the image is null (LipschitzWith.hausdorffMeasure_image_le). Countable subadditivity then applies (measure_biUnion_null_iff, measure_iUnion_null).
- Flatness. Let x ∈ spt T ∖ F, β > 0 and R > 0.
  - Pick δ with B_δ(x) ⊆ U, a rational q ∈ (0, min(R/2, δ/3)), z ∈ D_set with |z − x| < q, and j with 1/(j + 1) < β. Then (z, q) ∈ 𝒞.
  - Put w := q^{−1}(x − z). Then w ∈ B_1(0) ∩ spt μ₀ (support relation) and w ∉ Z_{z,q,j}.
  - class_reduction gives ρ₀, Q and s < ρ₀/(j + 1) with B_{ρ₀}(w) ⊆ B_2(0). Comparing diameters gives ρ₀ ≤ 2, so ρ := qρ₀ < R.
  - For y' ∈ spt T with |y' − x| < ρ, put y := q^{−1}(y' − z). Then y ∈ B_{ρ₀}(w) ∩ spt μ₀, and |(y' − x) − p_Q(y' − x)| = q|q_Q(y − w)| ≤ qs < βρ.

Basic facts. (F1) (Boundaries of blow-ups.) Let V ⊆ ℝ^P, A ∈ 𝒟_n(V) with ∂A = 0 in V (n ≥ 1), a ∈ ℝ^P and t > 0. By the contract's definition, blowUp A a t is the affine push-forward of the restriction of A to η_{a,t}^{−1}(η_{a,t}(V)) = V. The boundary commutes with the affine push-forward (SimonGMT GeometricCurrentOn.boundary_affinePushforward) and with restriction of the domain (both sides evaluate A on dω). Hence ∂(η_{a,t#}A) = η_{a,t#}(∂A) = 0, i.e. BoundaryVanishes (η_{a,t#}A). (F2) (blowup_scaling.) Let V be open, A ∈ 𝒟_n(V), a ∈ ℝ^P, t > 0, n ≥ 1. (2) If R represents A, some IMRep R' of η_{a,t#}A has R'.measure = (R.measure)^{a,t} (the Borel-set identity of blowup_scaling (2) and Measure.ext). (3) If A is minimizing in A₀ ⊆ ℝ^P, then η_{a,t#}A is minimizing in η_{a,t}(A₀). (F3) (ℝ^P as a submanifold.) ℝ^P is an embedded C² (n+k)-dimensional submanifold of itself: for every point take V = W = ℝ^P and ψ = id, which is open, C² and injective, with ψ(V) = W ∩ ℝ^P, V ∩ ψ^{−1}(K) = K compact for compact K, and Dψ = id injective. Also (closure ℝ^P ∖ ℝ^P) ∩ ℝ^P = ∅. So (MON) and (DTC) apply to a current minimizing in ℝ^P with U = N = ℝ^P, d := n + k, ℓ := k (U ∩ N = ℝ^P, spt ⊆ ℝ^P). (F4) (Vanishing off the support.) If A has open domain V and x ∈ V ∖ spt A, then x lies in the zero region of A (spt A = V ∖ zeroRegion A). So there is ε > 0 with B_ε(x) ⊆ V and μ_A(B_ε(x)) = 0 (IM-b, shrinking ε). Consequently, if t_j > 0 and t_j → 0, then μ_A^{x,t_j}(B_{ε/t_j}(0)) = t_j^{−n}μ_A(B_ε(x)) = 0. So ∫ f dμ_A^{x,t_j} = 0 as soon as tsupport f ⊆ B_{ε/t_j}(0), and ∫ f dμ_A^{x,t_j} → 0 for f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P). (F5) (Cone weights.) Let C ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) be a cone and R represent C. Then cone_measure_homogeneous gives μ_C(t·A) = t^nμ_C(A) for t > 0 and Borel A. Hence μ_C(B_ρ(tw)) = μ_C(t·B_{ρ/t}(w)) = t^nμ_C(B_{ρ/t}(w)), so the density ratio of μ_C at (tw, ρ) equals the ratio at (w, ρ/t). Since ρ ↦ ρ/t maps 𝓝[>]0 onto 𝓝[>]0, the limsups agree: dens μ_C(tw) = dens μ_C(w). (F6) (Uniqueness of vague limits.) If μ, ν are finite on compact sets and ∫ f dμ = ∫ f dν for all f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P), then μ = ν. Proof: let O be open and m ≥ 1; put f_m(x) := min(1, m·infDist(x, Oᶜ))·min(1, (m − |x|)⁺) if O ≠ ℝ^P and f_m(x) := min(1, (m − |x|)⁺) if O = ℝ^P. Each f_m is continuous with support in closedBall 0 m, 0 ≤ f_m ≤ 1_O, and f_m ↑ 1_O pointwise (for x ∈ O, infDist(x, Oᶜ) > 0 since Oᶜ is closed; for x ∉ O, f_m(x) = 0). By monotone convergence, μ(O) = lim_m ∫ f_m dμ = lim_m ∫ f_m dν = ν(O). Open sets form a π-system (isPiSystem_isOpen) generating the Borel σ-algebra (borel α is by definition generateFrom {s | IsOpen s}, and BorelSpace.measurable_eq), and the open balls B_m(0), m ∈ ℕ, are open sets of finite measure covering ℝ^P, so μ = ν (Measure.ext_of_generateFrom_of_iUnion). (F7) (Weak limits of blow-ups of cycles are cycles.) Let V ⊆ ℝ^P be open, A ∈ 𝒟_n(V) with ∂A = 0 in V, p ∈ V, s_j > 0 with s_j → 0, and C ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) with η_{p,s_j#}A ⇀ C in ℝ^P (ConvergesWeakly). Then ∂C = 0. Proof: write n = m + 1 and let ω ∈ 𝒟^m(ℝ^P), with tsupport ω ⊆ B_R(0). Then dω ∈ 𝒟^n(ℝ^P) and tsupport dω ⊆ tsupport ω (dω vanishes on the open set where ω vanishes). Choose δ > 0 with B_δ(p) ⊆ V. Then η_{p,s_j}(V) ⊇ η_{p,s_j}(B_δ(p)) = B_{δ/s_j}(0) ⊇ closedBall 0 R for all large j. For such j, ω and dω are test forms on η_{p,s_j}(V), so currentEval(η_{p,s_j#}A, dω) = (η_{p,s_j#}A)(dω) = ∂(η_{p,s_j#}A)(ω) = 0 by (F1). By ConvergesWeakly, C(dω) = lim_j currentEval(η_{p,s_j#}A, dω) = 0, i.e. (∂C)(ω) = 0. Hence ∂C = 0 (BoundaryVanishes C). (F8) (The zero current.) It is minimizing in ℝ^P (M_W(0) = 0 ≤ M_W(S') for every competitor S') and ∂0 = 0, and dens 0 ≡ 0. (F9) (Density representation; parent step 2 (iii), Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.8(2) and Theorem 1.9.) Let V ⊆ ℝ^P and R ∈ IMRep V n with R.measure(K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ ℝ^P. Then R.measure = Hⁿ.withDensity(ofReal ∘ dens(R.measure)). At such x, the limsup along the nontrivial filter 𝓝[>]0 equals the limit (Filter.Tendsto.limsup_eq). As g(x) ≠ ∞, ofReal(dens(R.measure)(x)) = ofReal(toReal(g(x))) = g(x) (ENNReal.ofReal_toReal). So ofReal ∘ dens(R.measure) = g Hⁿ-a.e. Hence Hⁿ.withDensity(ofReal ∘ dens(R.measure)) = Hⁿ.withDensity(g) (withDensity_congr_ae) = (Hⁿ.restrict R.carrier).withDensity(R.mult) (withDensity_indicator, R.carrier measurable) = R.measure (definition of IMRep.measure).

Since D(μ_S) = ℝ^P, μ_{j_i} = μ_{x_i,λ_i} with (x_i, λ_i) ∈ Par. As G_{x_i,λ_i} ⊇ B_{1/λ_i}(0) (3(d)) and K ⊆ B_{R_K}(0) for some R_K > 0, λ_i ≥ λ₀ := 1/R_K. The set {(x, λ) ∈ Par : λ ≥ λ₀} is compact, so along a further subsequence (x_i, λ_i) → (x*, λ*) in it. By 3(g), μ_{x_i,λ_i} → μ_{x*,λ*} vaguely; also μ_{x_i,λ_i} → μ vaguely. By (F6) (all finite on compact sets, (M1)), μ = μ_{x*,λ*}, so D μ = G_{x*,λ*} = B_{2/λ*}(−x*/λ*). The compact K lies in this open ball, so K ⊆ B_{2/λ*−ε}(−x*/λ*) for some ε > 0. 13. (M7) Let μ ∈ 𝓜, y ∈ spt μ, ρ > 0 with closedBall y ρ ⊆ D μ. If μ = μ_S: y ∈ spt S by (IM-b), so (c1) gives μ(B_ρ(y)) ≥ ω_nρ^n ≥ e^{−Λρ}ω_nρ^n (Λ ≥ 0). If μ = μ_{x,λ}: put p := z + r(x + λy). Then 1(d) with σ := rλρ gives μ(B_ρ(y)) = (rλ)^{−n}μ_T(B_{rλρ}(p)) ≥ (rλ)^{−n}e^{−Λ_Krλρ}ω_n(rλρ)^n = e^{−Λ_Krλρ}ω_nρ^n ≥ e^{−Λρ}ω_nρ^n (λ ≤ 1, Λ_K ≥ 0).

Let y ∈ L, t > 0, w ∈ ℝ^P and HasMassDensity S w θ. By 4(c2), θ = dens ν(w) = dens ν(y + tw) = Θ_S(y + tw), and HasMassDensity S (y + tw) Θ_S(y + tw) by 4(c); so HasMassDensity S (y + tw) θ. Thus the density of S is invariant as (PS) requires. (PS) applies (n ≤ n + k = P, dim L + 1 = n, S minimizing in ℝ^P, ∂S = 0) and gives an n-dimensional Q with spt S ⊆ Q. proof_key_steps: (MON) on K = closedBall z (2r) gives lower density bounds at support points of T; μ₀ is the rescaled restriction of μ_T to B_{2r}(z).
Positive-scale members μ_{x,λ} = λ^{−n}(η_{x,λ})_#μ₀ with domains η_{x,λ}(B_2(0)); the parameters are recovered from total mass and barycenter.
Zero-scale members are the weights of all minimizing cycles of ℝ^P: closed under blow-ups (blowup_scaling, ∂ commutes with push-forward), weight 0 or ∞, density ≥ ω_nρ^n on balls at support points.

Tangent measures: (DTC)(2) at support points (of T, or of a minimizing cycle with U = N = ℝ^P) gives minimizing cones, which are cycles because ∂ passes to weak limits; off the support the limit is 0; cone weights are homogeneous.
(M2) from (DEM); (M6) from compactness of the parameter set and uniqueness of vague limits; (M7) from monotonicity; (M9) from homogeneity forcing total mass 0 or ∞; (M8) from (PS).

subproblems.title: Flatness off a μH[n−2+α]-null set for an abstract measure class with domains, via Appendix A.4 (parent steps 3–4)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ with n ≥ 1, Λ ∈ ℝ, let 𝓜 be a set of measures on ℝ^P and D a map from measures on ℝ^P to subsets of ℝ^P. For a measure μ on ℝ^P and x ∈ ℝ^P let dens μ x := (limsup_{ρ↓0} μ(B_ρ(x))/(ω_nρ^n)).toReal (limsup in [0, ∞] along ρ → 0⁺, ω_n = unitBallVolume n; in the Lean statement dens is a universally quantified function fixed by this defining equation); for y ∈ ℝ^P and λ > 0, μ^{y,λ} := ofReal(λ^{−n})•μ.map(η_{y,λ}) (= λ^{−n}(η_{y,λ})_#μ, η_{y,λ} = dilation y λ); spt μ := {w : μ(B_ε(w)) ≠ 0 for every ε > 0}; μ_j → μ vaguely means ∫ f dμ_j → ∫ f dμ for every continuous compactly supported f : ℝ^P → ℝ. Assume (M1) every μ ∈ 𝓜 is finite on compact sets; (M2) every μ ∈ 𝓜 equals Hⁿ.withDensity(ofReal ∘ dens μ) (Hⁿ = μHE[n]); (M3) for μ ∈ 𝓜, 0 < λ < 1 and |y| ≤ 1 − λ: μ^{y,λ} ∈ 𝓜 and D(μ^{y,λ}) = η_{y,λ}(D μ); (M4) for μ ∈ 𝓜, |y| < 1 and every strictly decreasing sequence λ_j > 0 with λ_j → 0 there are a strictly increasing sub : ℕ → ℕ and ν ∈ 𝓜 with dens ν(tw) = dens ν(w) for all t > 0 and w, and μ^{y,λ_{sub(j)}} → ν vaguely; (M5) for μ ∈ 𝓜, D μ is open and contains B_2(0); (M6) if μ ∈ 𝓜, μ_j ∈ 𝓜 (j ∈ ℕ) and μ_j → μ vaguely, then every compact K ⊆ D μ satisfies K ⊆ D(μ_j) for all large j; (M7) for μ ∈ 𝓜, y ∈ spt μ and ρ > 0 with closedBall y ρ ⊆ D μ: e^{−Λρ}·ω_nρ^n ≤ μ(B_ρ(y)); (M8) if ν ∈ 𝓜 and L is a linear subspace with dim L + 1 = n and dens ν(y + tw) = dens ν(w) for all y ∈ L, t > 0 and w, then spt ν ⊆ Q for some n-dimensional linear subspace Q; (M9) if ν ∈ 𝓜 and dens ν(tw) = dens ν(w) for all t > 0 and w, then D ν = ℝ^P. Then for every μ ∈ 𝓜 and every β > 0 there is a set Z ⊆ ℝ^P such that Z = ∅ if n = 1, μH[n − 2 + α](Z) = 0 for every real α > 0, and every w ∈ B_1(0) ∩ spt μ with w ∉ Z is β-flat in D μ: there are ρ > 0 with B_ρ(w) ⊆ D μ, an n-dimensional linear subspace Q ⊆ ℝ^P and s < βρ such that |(y − w) − p_Q(y − w)| ≤ s for every y ∈ spt μ ∩ B_ρ(w) (p_Q = Q.starProjection).

Source: parent proof steps 2 (density functions (i)–(vii) and (T3s)), 3 (the flatness maps: closedness, A.3(1)–(3)) and 4 (Appendix A.4 and the exclusion of d = n − 1); Simon 7.3.3, Remark 3.4 and proof of 3.3(2), chapter-07.txt lines 485–583, with the parent's errata (in R_β the bound is sup|q(y − x)| < βρ; ∩_j instead of ∪_j in (12), (13)) and departure [D1] (scalar density functions; the domain of a member enters through D). Here the class properties (M1)–(M9) replace the parent's analysis of the currents; the arguments are those of the parent. Uses the reused accepted declaration abstract_dimension_reduction (Submission.abstract_dimension_reduction).
Notation. e₁ := EuclideanSpace.single 0 1 ∈ Euclid 1 (|e₁| = 1); φ_μ(x) := dens μ x • e₁; Hⁿ := μHE[n] = c•μH[n] with c := addHaarScalarFactor(volume, μH[n]) ∈ ℝ≥0, c ≠ 0 (euclideanHausdorffMeasure_def, addHaarScalarFactor_volume_hausdorffMeasure_ne_zero); μ^{y,t}, spt, vague convergence as in the statement; q_Q(v) := v − p_Q(v) (|q_Q(v)| ≤ |v|). Fix β > 0. For μ ∈ 𝓜 let R(μ) be the set of w ∈ spt μ for which there are ρ > 0 with B_ρ(w) ⊆ D μ, an n-dimensional Q and s < βρ with |q_Q(y − w)| ≤ s for all y ∈ spt μ ∩ B_ρ(w) ('β-flat points'), and sing'(μ) := ((spt μ ∩ D μ) ∖ R(μ)) ∪ (ℝ^P ∖ D μ).
1. (Measurability of dens μ, any measure μ.) For ρ > 0, x ↦ μ(B_ρ(x)) is lower semicontinuous: if x_j → x then 1_{B_ρ(x)} ≤ liminf_j 1_{B_ρ(x_j)} pointwise, so μ(B_ρ(x)) ≤ liminf μ(B_ρ(x_j)) (Fatou). Hence g_ρ(x) := μ(B_ρ(x))/(ω_nρ^n) and G_m := sup_{0<ρ<1/(m+1)} g_ρ are lower semicontinuous (suprema of lsc functions), hence Borel. As the intervals (0, 1/(m+1)) form a basis of 𝓝[>]0 and G_m decreases in m, limsup_{ρ→0⁺} g_ρ(x) = inf_m G_m(x) (Filter.HasBasis.limsup_eq_iInf_iSup) is Borel, so dens μ is Borel measurable, and dens μ ≥ 0.
2. (Normalization.) For μ ∈ 𝓜, (M2) and Hⁿ = c•μH[n] give μ = c•(μH[n].withDensity(ofReal ∘ dens μ)). Hence (a) ∫⁻_A ofReal(dens μ) dμH[n] = c^{−1}μ(A) for Borel A; (b) for f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P), f·dens μ is μH[n]-integrable (by (a) on a ball containing tsupport f and (M1)) and ∫ f·dens μ dμH[n] = c^{−1}∫ f dμ (integral_withDensity_eq_integral_smul with the measurable ℝ≥0-valued density of step 1); (c) ∫ f·φ_μ dμH[n] = (c^{−1}∫ f dμ)•e₁ (integral_smul_const).
3. (Rescaling, any measure μ, y ∈ ℝ^P, t > 0.) μ^{y,t}(B_ρ(w)) = t^{−n}μ(B_{tρ}(y + tw)) (η_{y,t}^{−1}(B_ρ(w)) = B_{tρ}(y + tw), Measure.map_apply), so the density ratio of μ^{y,t} at (w, ρ) equals that of μ at (y + tw, tρ); since ρ ↦ tρ maps 𝓝[>]0 onto 𝓝[>]0, dens μ^{y,t}(w) = dens μ(y + tw), i.e. φ_{μ^{y,t}}(w) = φ_μ(y + tw); likewise spt μ^{y,t} = {w : y + tw ∈ spt μ}.
4. (The family.) F := {φ_μ : μ ∈ 𝓜} ⊆ (ℝ^P → Euclid 1). Injectivity: if φ_μ = φ_ν (μ, ν ∈ 𝓜) then dens μ = dens ν (e₁ ≠ 0), so μ = ν by (M2). Define sing(φ) := {w : ∃ μ ∈ 𝓜, φ = φ_μ ∧ w ∈ sing'(μ)}; by injectivity sing(φ_μ) = sing'(μ).
5. ((H0), (H1).) If φ_μ = φ_ν μH[n]-a.e., then dens μ = dens ν μH[n]-a.e., hence Hⁿ-a.e. (Hⁿ = c•μH[n]), so μ = ν by (M2) and withDensity_congr_ae, and φ_μ = φ_ν. φ_μ is measurable (step 1) and for every x, ∫_{B_1(x)} |φ_μ| dμH[n] = c^{−1}μ(B_1(x)) < ∞ (step 2(a), (M1) on closedBall x 1); so φ_μ is locally μH[n]-integrable.
6. (A.1.) For φ_μ ∈ F, 0 < λ < 1, |y| ≤ 1 − λ: φ_μ(y + λ·) = φ_{μ^{y,λ}} (step 3) and μ^{y,λ} ∈ 𝓜 (M3).
7. (A.2.) Let φ_μ ∈ F, |y| < 1, and λ_k > 0 strictly decreasing to 0. (M4) gives sub and ν ∈ 𝓜 with dens ν homogeneous and μ^{y,λ_{sub(k)}} → ν vaguely. For k ≥ k₀ (λ_{sub(k)} ≤ 1 − |y| and λ_{sub(k)} < 1), μ^{y,λ_{sub(k)}} ∈ 𝓜 by (M3), so by steps 3 and 2(c), for every f ∈ C_c: ∫ f(x)·φ_μ(y + λ_{sub(k)}x) dμH[n](x) = ∫ f·φ_{μ^{y,λ_{sub(k)}}} dμH[n] = (c^{−1}∫ f dμ^{y,λ_{sub(k)}})•e₁ → (c^{−1}∫ f dν)•e₁ = ∫ f·φ_ν dμH[n] (the finitely many k < k₀ do not affect the limit). ψ := φ_ν ∈ F, and ψ(tx) = ψ(x) for t > 0 by the homogeneity of dens ν.
8. (Support semicontinuity, parent (T3s).) If μ_k, μ ∈ 𝓜, μ_k → μ vaguely, y_k ∈ spt μ_k and y_k → y ∈ D μ, then y ∈ spt μ. Proof: D μ is open (M5), so closedBall y (3ρ₁) ⊆ D μ for some ρ₁ ∈ (0, 1]; by (M6) closedBall y (3ρ₁) ⊆ D μ_k for large k; also |y_k − y| < ρ₁ for large k, so closedBall y_k ρ ⊆ D μ_k for 0 < ρ ≤ ρ₁ and (M7) gives μ_k(B_ρ(y_k)) ≥ e^{−Λρ}ω_nρ^n. Let ε ∈ (0, ρ₁] and take f ∈ C_c with 0 ≤ f ≤ 1, f = 1 on closedBall y (ε/2) and tsupport f ⊆ B_ε(y). For large k, B_{ε/4}(y_k) ⊆ closedBall y (ε/2), so ∫ f dμ_k ≥ μ_k(B_{ε/4}(y_k)) ≥ e^{−Λε/4}ω_n(ε/4)^n. Hence μ(B_ε(y)) ≥ ∫ f dμ = lim ∫ f dμ_k ≥ e^{−Λε/4}ω_n(ε/4)^n > 0 (ω_n > 0); larger ε follow by monotonicity.
9. (A.3, closedness.) spt μ is closed (if μ(B_ε(w)) = 0 then μ(B_{ε/2}(w')) = 0 for w' ∈ B_{ε/2}(w)). R(μ) is relatively open in spt μ: if (ρ, Q, s) witnesses w ∈ R(μ) (s ≥ |q_Q(w − w)| = 0, as w ∈ spt μ ∩ B_ρ(w)), w' ∈ spt μ and t := |w' − w| satisfies (1 + β)t < βρ − s, then (ρ − t, Q, s + t) witnesses w' ∈ R(μ): ρ − t > 0, B_{ρ−t}(w') ⊆ B_ρ(w) ⊆ D μ, and for y ∈ spt μ ∩ B_{ρ−t}(w'), |q_Q(y − w')| ≤ |q_Q(y − w)| + |q_Q(w − w')| ≤ s + t < β(ρ − t). Hence sing'(μ) is closed: if w ∉ sing'(μ) then w ∈ D μ (open) and either w ∉ spt μ — then some ball around w lies in D μ and misses the closed set spt μ, hence misses sing'(μ) — or w ∈ R(μ) — then some ball B around w lies in D μ with B ∩ spt μ ⊆ R(μ), and no point of B is in sing'(μ).
10. (A.3(1).) Let φ_μ = 1_L·c' with dim L = n and c' ∈ Euclid 1. Then dens μ(x) = 0 for x ∉ L and dens μ(x) = a (the coordinate of c') for x ∈ L; in particular dens μ(tx) = dens μ(x) for t > 0 (tx ∈ L ⟺ x ∈ L), so D μ = ℝ^P by (M9). For w ∉ L there is ε > 0 with B_ε(w) ∩ L = ∅ (L is closed), and by (M2) μ(B_ε(w)) = ∫_{B_ε(w)} ofReal(dens μ) dHⁿ = 0; so spt μ ⊆ L. Every w ∈ spt μ lies in R(μ) with (ρ, Q, s) = (1, L, 0): B_1(w) ⊆ ℝ^P = D μ, and for y ∈ spt μ, y − w ∈ L, so q_L(y − w) = 0 and 0 < β. Hence sing(φ_μ) = sing'(μ) = ∅.
11. (A.3(2).) Let φ_μ ∈ F, 0 < λ < 1, |y| ≤ 1 − λ, μ' := μ^{y,λ} ∈ 𝓜 (M3) and g(w) := y + λw. Then φ_μ∘g = φ_{μ'} and spt μ' = g^{−1}(spt μ) (step 3), D μ' = η_{y,λ}(D μ) = g^{−1}(D μ) (M3; η_{y,λ} = g^{−1}), and R(μ') = g^{−1}(R(μ)): (ρ, Q, s) witnesses w ∈ R(μ') iff (λρ, Q, λs) witnesses g(w) ∈ R(μ), since g maps B_ρ(w) onto B_{λρ}(g(w)) and spt μ' ∩ B_ρ(w) onto spt μ ∩ B_{λρ}(g(w)), and q_Q(g(y) − g(w)) = λq_Q(y − w). 12. (A.3(3).) Let μ, μ_k ∈ 𝓜 with ∫ f·φ_{μ_k} dμH[n] → ∫ f·φ_μ dμH[n] for every f ∈ C_c; by step 2(c) (c ≠ 0, e₁ ≠ 0), μ_k → μ vaguely. Let ε > 0 and suppose that for infinitely many k there is w_k ∈ B_1(0) ∩ sing'(μ_k) with |w_k − z'| ≥ ε for every z' ∈ sing'(μ). As closedBall 0 1 ⊆ D μ (M5), step 8 gives w ∈ spt μ; |w − z'| ≥ ε for all z' ∈ sing'(μ), so w ∉ sing'(μ), and hence w ∈ R(μ), witnessed by (ρ, Q, s) with s < βρ. Choose ρ' ∈ (0, ρ) with s < βρ', put τ := (s + βρ')/2 ∈ (s, βρ') and choose η ∈ (0, (ρ − ρ')/2). 13. (Appendix A.4.) By steps 4–12, abstract_dimension_reduction applies to (P, n, Q := 1, F, sing). Hence either (I) B_1(0) ∩ sing'(μ) = ∅ for every μ ∈ 𝓜, or (II) there is d ∈ ℕ with d + 1 ≤ n such that μH[d + α](sing'(μ) ∩ B_1(0)) = 0 for every μ ∈ 𝓜 and α > 0, and there are ν ∈ 𝓜 and a d-dimensional subspace L with sing'(ν) = L and φ_ν(y + tx) = φ_ν(x) for y ∈ L, t > 0 and all x.

Then dens ν(y + tx) = dens ν(x) for y ∈ L, t > 0 (e₁ ≠ 0); in particular (y = 0) dens ν is homogeneous, so D ν = ℝ^P by (M9), and (M8) gives an n-dimensional Q with spt ν ⊆ Q. Every w ∈ spt ν lies in R(ν) with (1, Q, 0) (y − w ∈ Q for y, w ∈ Q), so sing'(ν) = ((spt ν ∩ ℝ^P) ∖ R(ν)) ∪ ∅ = ∅ ≠ L (0 ∈ L): a contradiction. Hence in case (II), d + 2 ≤ n.
15. (Conclusion.) Fix μ ∈ 𝓜 and put Z := sing'(μ) ∩ B_1(0). In case (I), Z = ∅, so μH[s](Z) = 0 for every s. In case (II), d + 2 ≤ n, so n ≥ 2 and, for α > 0, n − 2 + α = d + α' with α' := n − 2 − d + α > 0, whence μH[n − 2 + α](Z) = 0. If n = 1, case (II) is impossible (d + 2 ≤ 1 fails), so Z = ∅. If ψ ∈ F is L-invariant with dim L ≥ n, then ψ = ψ(0)·1_{L'} for an n-dimensional L' ⊆ L and sing ψ = ∅: for x ∉ L', ψ ≡ ψ(x) on the relatively open half {y+λx : y ∈ L', λ>0} of an (n+1)-plane, which has infinite H^n-measure near each of its points, so local integrability forces ψ(x) = 0; ψ(y) = ψ(0) on L'. 4. If some sing φ meets B_1(0), let 𝒟 := {dim L : some L-invariant ψ ∈ F has sing ψ ≠ ∅}. Lemma T with A.2 gives a homogeneous ψ with 0 ∈ sing ψ, so 0 ∈ 𝒟; by step 3 elements of 𝒟 are ≤ n−1. Put d := max 𝒟 (so n ≥ 1; if n = 0 the first alternative holds).

Proof: by (d) choose λ_k ↓ 0, λ_k ≤ (1−|x|)/2, with h^ℓ_∞(A ∩ B_{λ_k}(x)) ≥ (c_ℓ/2)λ_k^ℓ, and ψ by A.2. K := B̄_1(0) ∖ ∪B_{ρ_j}(x_j) is compact and disjoint from the closed set sing ψ; by A.3(3), for large k, B_1(0) ∩ sing φ_{x,λ_k} ⊆ ∪B_{ρ_j}(x_j), so h^ℓ_∞(B_1(0) ∩ sing φ_{x,λ_k}) < ε. By A.3(2) this set is λ_k^{−1}(A ∩ B_{λ_k}(x) − x), so h^ℓ_∞(A ∩ B_{λ_k}(x)) < ελ_k^ℓ: a contradiction for ε < c_ℓ/2.

Proof: homogeneous ψ has ψ_{w,1} = ψ_{θw,θ} ∈ F for θ = 1/(2+|w|) (A.1). For y ∈ S, (φ_{x,λ_k})_{y,1} = φ_{x,λ_k}, so ψ_{y,1} = ψ by (b), (a). For β ∈ ℝ, homogeneity of φ gives (φ_{x,λ_k})_{βx,1} = (φ_{x,λ_k})_{0,μ_k}, μ_k = (1+βλ_k)^{−1} → 1, so by (b), (c), (a) ψ_{βx,1} = ψ. Combine with homogeneity.

Otherwise step 5 gives a homogeneous φ¹ ∈ F^ℓ; given φ ∈ F^ℓ invariant under a j-dimensional S, j ≤ d < ℓ, H^ℓ(S) = 0 lets us pick x ∉ S in the good set of step 5, and Lemma I gives ψ ∈ F^ℓ invariant under S+ℝx. subproblems.title: Mass of an integer multiplicity current equals its representing measure; support = support of that measure (reused accepted declaration)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let U ⊆ ℝ^P (= Euclid P) be open, let T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) (GeometricCurrentOn U n) and let R = (M, θ, ξ) be an integer multiplicity representation of T in U (an IMRep U n with R.Represents T, i.e. T(ω) = ∫_M θ(x)·ξ(x)(ω(x)) dH^n(x) for every ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U), where H^n = μHE[n]). Write μ_R := R.measure = θ·H^n⌞M. Then: (a) M_W(T) = μ_R(W) for every open W ⊆ U, where M_W(T) = T.massOn W is the supremum (in [0, ∞]) of ofReal T(ω) over ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ W and Euclidean coefficient norm |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x; (b) for every x ∈ U: x ∈ spt T if and only if μ_R(B_ε(x)) ≠ 0 for every ε > 0; (c) every other representation R' of T has the same measure: R'.measure = R.measure.

Source: Simon Ch. 6, 2.4–2.8 and Remark 3.2(3) (chapter-06.txt lines 224–300 and 733–775), which state these facts as evident; this is the identity "μ_S = R.measure for every representation R, M_W(S) = μ_S(W), spt S = spt μ_S" used throughout the parent proof (its Notation paragraph). Notation: H^n := μHE[n]; for an n-covector α on ℝ^P, |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α = (Σ_I α(e_{i_1}, …, e_{i_n})²)^{1/2}, the sum over strictly increasing multi-indices I = (i_1 < ⋯ < i_n) (for n = 0, |α| = |α()|); dx^I is the dual basis covector.
1. (Pointwise duality.) Let τ_1, …, τ_n ∈ ℝ^P be orthonormal and let α be an n-covector. By multilinearity and alternation, α(τ_1, …, τ_n) = Σ_I α(e_I)·det(τ^I), where τ^I is the n × n matrix (⟨e_{i_a}, τ_b⟩)_{a,b}. By the Cauchy–Binet formula, Σ_I det(τ^I)² = det(τᵀτ) = det(I_n) = 1. Hence |α(τ_1, …, τ_n)| ≤ |α| by the Cauchy–Schwarz inequality, with equality for α_τ := Σ_I det(τ^I) dx^I, which satisfies |α_τ| = 1 and α_τ(τ_1, …, τ_n) = 1. (For n = 0 both sides equal |α()| and α_τ := 1.)
2. (Consequences for R.) By the field `orients` of IMRep, for H^n-a.e. x ∈ M there are an orthonormal family τ(x) and a sign σ(x) ∈ {±1} with ξ(x)(α) = σ(x)·α(τ(x)) for every n-covector α (IsUnitOrientationOf). Hence, for H^n-a.e. x ∈ M, |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for all α. Moreover β(x) := Σ_I ξ(x)(dx^I)·dx^I equals σ(x)·α_{τ(x)} for H^n-a.e. x ∈ M, so |β(x)| = 1 and ξ(x)(β(x)) = 1 there. The coefficients ξ(·)(dx^I) of β are H^n⌞M-measurable because ξ is AEStronglyMeasurable for H^n⌞M (field aestronglyMeasurable_orient); as μ_R ≪ H^n⌞M, β is μ_R-measurable.
3. (Radon property.) μ_R is a Borel measure on ℝ^P with μ_R(ℝ^P ∖ U) = 0 (M ⊆ U) and μ_R(K) = ∫_{M∩K} θ dH^n < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U (field locallyIntegrable_mult). Since U is an open subset of ℝ^P, hence σ-compact, locally compact and second countable, the restriction of μ_R to U is a locally finite Borel measure on U and therefore outer regular by open sets and inner regular by compact sets on Borel subsets of U.
4. (Upper bound in (a).) Let W ⊆ U be open and let ω be admissible for M_W(T) (ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U), tsupport ω ⊆ W, |ω| ≤ 1 everywhere). By R.Represents T and step 2, T(ω) = ∫_M θ·ξ(ω) dH^n ≤ ∫_M θ·|ω| dH^n ≤ ∫_{M∩W} θ dH^n = μ_R(W), because ω vanishes off W. Taking ofReal and the supremum, M_W(T) ≤ μ_R(W).
5. (Lower bound in (a).) Let W ⊆ U be open, K ⊆ W compact and ε > 0. By step 3 choose an open V with K ⊆ V, closure V compact and contained in W, and μ_R(V ∖ K) < ε. By Lusin's theorem (for the finite Radon measure μ_R⌞V and the μ_R-measurable map β of step 2, with values in the finite-dimensional space Λ^n of n-covectors) choose a compact K' ⊆ K with μ_R(K ∖ K') < ε and β|_{K'} continuous. Extend β|_{K'} to a continuous map ℝ^P → Λ^n (Tietze, coordinatewise) and compose with the retraction r(α) := α / max(1, |α|) (continuous, |r(α)| ≤ 1, r = id on the closed unit ball) to obtain a continuous β̃ with |β̃| ≤ 1 and β̃ = β on K'. Take χ ∈ C_c(V; [0, 1]) with χ = 1 on K, and put γ := χ·β̃ (continuous, |γ| ≤ 1, compact support in V). Let γ_j := γ * ϱ_{1/j} be the coordinatewise convolution with a standard mollifier. For all large j, γ_j is C^∞, tsupport γ_j is a compact subset of V ⊆ W ⊆ U, |γ_j| ≤ 1 everywhere (Jensen's inequality for the convex function |·|), and γ_j → γ uniformly. So γ_j is admissible for M_W(T) and M_W(T) ≥ ofReal T(γ_j). By dominated convergence (dominating function θ·1_{closure V}, integrable by step 3), T(γ_j) = ∫_M θ·ξ(γ_j) dH^n → ∫_M θ·ξ(γ) dH^n. On K', ξ(γ) = ξ(β) = 1 μ_R-a.e.; on V ∖ K', |ξ(γ)| ≤ 1; off V, γ = 0. Hence ∫_M θ·ξ(γ) dH^n ≥ μ_R(K') − μ_R(V ∖ K') ≥ (μ_R(K) − ε) − 2ε, since μ_R(V ∖ K') ≤ μ_R(V ∖ K) + μ_R(K ∖ K') < 2ε. Therefore M_W(T) ≥ μ_R(K) − 3ε for every compact K ⊆ W and every ε > 0, and inner regularity of μ_R on the open set W (step 3) gives M_W(T) ≥ μ_R(W) (also when μ_R(W) = ∞). Together with step 4, M_W(T) = μ_R(W).
6. ((b), "if".) Let x ∈ U with μ_R(B_ε(x)) ≠ 0 for every ε > 0, and suppose x ∉ spt T = U ∖ zeroRegion(T). Then x ∈ W for some open W with closure W compact and contained in U on which T vanishes, i.e. T(ω) = 0 whenever tsupport ω ⊆ W. Every admissible value in the definition of M_W(T) is ofReal 0 = 0 (and the zero form is admissible), so M_W(T) = 0, and by (a) μ_R(W) = 0. For ε > 0 so small that B_ε(x) ⊆ W we get μ_R(B_ε(x)) = 0, a contradiction. Hence x ∈ spt T.
7. ((b), "only if".) Let x ∈ spt T and suppose μ_R(B_ε(x)) = 0 for some ε > 0. Choose ε' ∈ (0, ε) with closedBall x ε' ⊆ U (U is open). W := B_{ε'}(x) is open, its closure closedBall x ε' is compact and contained in U, and for every ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ W, step 2 gives |T(ω)| ≤ ∫_{M∩W} θ·|ω| dH^n ≤ (sup_x |ω(x)|)·μ_R(W) = 0. So T vanishes on W, W belongs to the family defining zeroRegion(T), x ∈ zeroRegion(T), i.e. x ∉ spt T: a contradiction. Hence μ_R(B_ε(x)) ≠ 0 for every ε > 0.
8. ((c).) Let R' be another representation of T. By (a) applied to R and to R', R'.measure(W) = M_W(T) = R.measure(W) for every open W ⊆ U. Both measures vanish on ℝ^P ∖ U (both carriers lie in U) and are finite on every open W whose closure is a compact subset of U (step 3). The open subsets of U with compact closure in U form a π-system (closed under finite intersections) generating the Borel σ-algebra of U (every open subset of U is a countable union of them), and U is the union of an increasing sequence of them on which both measures are finite. By the uniqueness theorem for measures agreeing on such a generating π-system, R'.measure(A ∩ U) = R.measure(A ∩ U) for every Borel A, hence R'.measure = R.measure.
proof_key_steps: Cauchy–Binet duality: |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for the unit simple orientation ξ(x), with equality for the dual covector β(x).
Upper bound M_W(T) ≤ μ_R(W) directly from the representation.
Lower bound by Lusin, Tietze extension, retraction to the unit ball, mollification and inner regularity of the Radon measure μ_R.
Support: T vanishes on W ⇔ M_W(T) = 0 ⇔ μ_R(W) = 0, giving spt T = spt μ_R inside U.
Representation independence: two representations agree on open subsets of U, hence (π-system uniqueness, σ-finiteness on U) everywhere.

The numbered proof below is that node's independently reviewed parent-supplied proof, reproduced unchanged; its 'parent'/'sibling' references are to that node's own parent and siblings.

Source: Simon Ch. 6, 2.23–2.24 (push-forward, chapter-06.txt lines 405–440) and 3.3–3.9 (push-forward of integer multiplicity currents, lines 770–862); the scaling identity (1) in the proof of Simon 7.3.1 (chapter-07.txt lines 329–331); invariance of minimality under dilations is used in the proof of 7.3.1 (line 333) and in step 4(iv) of the parent proof ("dilations preserve minimality").
0. Facts about η. η is an affine bijection of ℝ^P with inverse η⁻¹(z) = x + λz and |η(y) − η(y')| = λ⁻¹|y − y'|.
 (i) Hⁿ(η(E)) = λ^{−n}Hⁿ(E) for every E ⊆ ℝ^P (Hⁿ = μHE[n] is translation invariant and Hⁿ(cE) = cⁿHⁿ(E) for c > 0: Mathlib euclideanHausdorffMeasure_smul₀, euclideanHausdorffMeasure_homothety_image). Hence for Borel E and Borel g ≥ 0 (or g integrable on η(E)): ∫_{η(E)} g dHⁿ = λ^{−n}∫_E g∘η dHⁿ.
 (ii) The pullback is (η^#ω)(y)(v₁,…,vₙ) = ω(η(y))(λ⁻¹v₁,…,λ⁻¹vₙ) = λ^{−n}ω(η(y))(v₁,…,vₙ); so η^#ω = λ^{−n}(ω∘η), |η^#ω(y)| = λ^{−n}|ω(η(y))| for the Euclidean coefficient norm, and tsupport η^#ω = η⁻¹(tsupport ω). By the definition of blowUp (affine push-forward of the restriction of T, with η⁻¹(η(U)) = U), S(ω) = T(η^#ω) for ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(η(U)). Conversely every ω' ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) equals η^#ω for exactly one ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(η(U)), namely ω = λⁿ(ω'∘η⁻¹). The same statements hold for any current Y ∈ 𝒟_n(U) and its push-forward η_#Y(ω) := Y(η^#ω).
 (iii) If ζ(α) = ±α(τ) then ζ(λ^{−n}α) = λ^{−n}ζ(α) (linearity).
1. Mass scaling. Let Y ∈ 𝒟_n(U) and W ⊆ ℝ^P. The map ω ↦ ω∘η = λⁿη^#ω is a bijection from the admissible forms for η_#Y on η(W) (ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(η(U)), tsupport ω ⊆ η(W), |ω| ≤ 1) onto the admissible forms for Y on W (tsupport(ω∘η) = η⁻¹(tsupport ω) ⊆ η⁻¹(η(W)) = W and |ω(η(y))| ≤ 1), and η_#Y(ω) = Y(η^#ω) = λ^{−n}Y(ω∘η). Since ofReal(λ^{−n}t) = ofReal(λ^{−n})·ofReal(t) and multiplication by the finite constant ofReal(λ^{−n}) commutes with suprema in [0, ∞], M_{η(W)}(η_#Y) = ofReal(λ^{−n})·M_W(Y). With Y = T this is (1).
2. Representation. Let R = (M, θ, ξ) represent T and define R' := (M', θ', ξ') with M' := η(M), θ' := θ∘η⁻¹, ξ' := ξ∘η⁻¹.
 - M' is Borel (image of a Borel set under a homeomorphism of ℝ^P) and M' ⊆ η(U).
 - M' is countably n-rectifiable: if M ⊆ M₀ ∪ ⋃_j F_j(ℝⁿ) with Hⁿ(M₀) = 0 and F_j Lipschitz, then M' ⊆ η(M₀) ∪ ⋃_j (η∘F_j)(ℝⁿ), Hⁿ(η(M₀)) = 0 by 0(i), and each η∘F_j is Lipschitz.
 - θ' is measurable, ℕ-valued, and θ' ≥ 1 on M'.
 - For compact K ⊆ η(U), η⁻¹(K) is a compact subset of U and ∫_{M'∩K} θ' dHⁿ = λ^{−n}∫_{M∩η⁻¹(K)} θ dHⁿ < ∞ by 0(i).
 - ξ' is a.e. strongly measurable for Hⁿ⌞M' (composition with the homeomorphism η⁻¹, which carries Hⁿ⌞M'-null sets to Hⁿ⌞M-null sets by 0(i)).
 - Orientation: let y ∈ M be such that Q := T_yM exists and ξ(y) orients Q (Hⁿ-a.e. y ∈ M), and z := η(y). For r > 0 and w ∈ ℝ^P, η_{z,r}(η(w)) = (η(w) − η(y))/r = (w − y)/(λr) = η_{y,λr}(w), so η_{z,r}(M') = η_{y,λr}(M) and ∫_{η_{z,r}(M')} f dHⁿ = ∫_{η_{y,λr}(M)} f dHⁿ → ∫_Q f dHⁿ as r ↓ 0 for every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P). Hence HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M' z Q, and ξ'(z) = ξ(y) orients Q. The exceptional set in M' is the η-image of an Hⁿ-null set, hence null.
 - Representation: for ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(η(U)), by 0(ii),(iii) and 0(i): S(ω) = T(η^#ω) = ∫_M θ(y)ξ(y)(λ^{−n}ω(η(y))) dHⁿ(y) = λ^{−n}∫_M (θ'·ξ'(ω))(η(y)) dHⁿ(y) = ∫_{M'} θ'(z)ξ'(z)(ω(z)) dHⁿ(z).
 - Measure: for Borel B, μ_{R'}(B) = ∫_{M'∩B} θ' dHⁿ = λ^{−n}∫_{M∩η⁻¹(B)} θ dHⁿ = ofReal(λ^{−n})·μ_R(η⁻¹(B)). This proves (2).
3. Minimality. Assume T is minimizing in A. By (2), S is integer multiplicity. Let W' be open with closure W' compact and ⊆ η(U), S' ∈ 𝒟_n(η(U)) integer multiplicity with ∂S' = ∂S (n ≥ 1), and spt(S' − S) a compact subset of η(A) ∩ W'.
 (a) Define S'' ∈ 𝒟_n(U) by S''(ω') := S'(λⁿ(ω'∘η⁻¹)), the push-forward of S' by the affine map η⁻¹. It is linear, and continuous because ω' ↦ λⁿ(ω'∘η⁻¹) maps convergent sequences in 𝒟ⁿ(U) to convergent sequences in 𝒟ⁿ(η(U)) (supports are mapped by the homeomorphism η, derivatives transform by the chain rule for the affine map). By 0(ii), S''(η^#ω) = S'(ω) for ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(η(U)), i.e. η_#S'' = S' (= blowUp S'' x λ); likewise T(ω') = S(λⁿ(ω'∘η⁻¹)), so S'' − T is the η⁻¹-push-forward of S' − S.

subproblems.statement: Let ℓ ≤ k, U ⊆ ℝ^{n+k} open, N an embedded C² (n+ℓ)-dimensional submanifold with (closure N ∖ N) ∩ U = ∅, and T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) with spt T ⊆ N, T minimizing in N ∩ U (Simon 7.1.1, integer multiplicity competitors) and ∂T = 0 in U (vacuous for n = 0). Then for every integer multiplicity representation R = (M, θ, ξ) of T, the varifold v(M, θ) is stationary in N ∩ U (∫_M θ div_M X dH^n = 0 for all X ∈ C¹_c(U; ℝ^{n+k}) with X(x) ∈ T_xN for x ∈ N ∩ U) and has a generalized mean curvature H in U that is μ_V-essentially bounded on every compact subset of U.

Throughout, μ_T = R.measure = θH^n⌞M for every representation (Ch. 6, 3.2(3); sibling child im_mass_measure (c)), and M_W(T) = μ_T(W) for open W (sibling child im_mass_measure (a)).
1. Case n = 0. Let R represent T and suppose x₀ ∈ M (H^0 is counting measure, so the a.e. conditions on R hold at every point of M; M is locally finite since ∫_{M∩K}θ dH^0 < ∞). Testing T with a 0-form supported near x₀ shows x₀ ∈ spt T ⊆ N. Let S be represented by (M∖{x₀}, θ, ξ); S is integer multiplicity, SameBoundary holds trivially (n = 0), spt(S−T) = {x₀} ⊆ N ∩ U ∩ W for a small open ball W ⊂⊂ U, and M_W(S) = M_W(T) − θ(x₀) < M_W(T), contradicting minimality. So M = ∅, the first variation vanishes identically, and H := 0 works. Assume n ≥ 1 from now on.
2. Support facts. μ_T(U ∖ spt T) = 0, hence H^n(M ∖ N) = 0. Since N is a C¹ submanifold, for H^n-a.e. x ∈ M the approximate tangent space T_xM exists, is the plane oriented by ξ(x) (definition of IMRep) and is contained in T_xN (approximate tangent spaces of subsets of a C¹ submanifold, Ch. 3 §1 and Ch. 2 §4); also div_M X(x) = trace(p_{T_xM}∘DX(x)) = tangentialDivergence (Ch. 4, 2.3).
3. Deformations (book: "φ = φ_t of 2.1 of Ch. 4 with U ∩ N in place of U"; Ch. 4, 2.5–2.6). Let X ∈ C¹_c(U; ℝ^{n+k}) be tangent to N on N ∩ U, K := spt X. X is globally Lipschitz, so it has a C¹ flow φ_t (t ∈ ℝ), each φ_t a C¹ diffeomorphism of U onto U with φ_t = id outside K. N ∩ U is relatively closed in U (because (N̄∖N) ∩ U = ∅) and X|_{N∩U} is a C¹ tangent field on the C² manifold N; integral curves of this tangent field are integral curves of X, so by uniqueness the orbit of a point of N ∩ U stays in N ∩ U (it cannot leave the relatively closed set N ∩ U while staying in K ∪ {x} ⊂ U). Hence φ_t(N ∩ U) ⊆ N ∩ U.
4. Competitors (book (2),(3)). Let S_t := φ_{t#}T, defined from the representation (Ch. 6, 2.24(2), 3.3–3.9): S_t = τ(φ_t(M), θ∘φ_t^{−1}, induced orientation), an integer multiplicity current in U. ∂S_t = 0: choose smooth diffeomorphisms φ^ε of U, equal to the identity outside a fixed compact set, with φ^ε → φ_t in C¹; then φ^ε_#T(dω) = T((φ^ε)^#dω) = T(d(φ^ε)^#ω) = 0 and φ^ε_#T(dω) → S_t(dω) by dominated convergence in the integral formula of 2.24(2). Since φ_t = id off K, spt T ⊆ N and φ_t(N ∩ U) ⊆ N ∩ U, spt(S_t − T) ⊆ K ∩ N is compact. For any open W with K ⊂ W ⊂⊂ U, minimality gives M_W(T) ≤ M_W(S_t) for all t.
5. First variation (book (1)). By the area formula (Ch. 6, 3.2(3), 3.3–3.5; Ch. 4, 1.7–1.8), M_W(S_t) = ∫_{M∩W} J^M φ_t θ dH^n. Since φ_t(x) = x + tX(x) + o(t) in C¹ uniformly on K, d/dt J^Mφ_t(x)|_{t=0} = div_M X(x) with uniform bounds on K, and θ is integrable on K; so t ↦ M_W(S_t) is differentiable at 0 with derivative ∫_M θ div_M X dH^n (Ch. 4, 2.2). The minimum at t = 0 forces this derivative to vanish: R.firstVariation X = 0. This is IsStationaryAlong N.
6. Mean curvature (Ch. 4, 2.7 and 3.14). Let X ∈ C¹_c(U; ℝ^{n+k}) be arbitrary. Choose an open V ⊂ U containing N ∩ spt X on which the nearest point projection π onto N is C¹ (N is C²), let P(z) be the orthogonal projection onto T_zN (C¹ in z ∈ N), χ ∈ C¹_c(V) with χ = 1 near N ∩ spt X, and X^T := χ·P(π(·))X. Then X^T ∈ C¹_c(U) is tangent to N on N ∩ U, so δV(X^T) = 0 by step 5. On N, X − X^T = X^⊥ is normal to N, and at H^n-a.e. x ∈ M (where T_xM ⊆ T_xN by step 2) div_M X^⊥ = −X·H_N(x), H_N(x) := Σ_{i=1}^n B_x(τ_i, τ_i) with τ_i an orthonormal basis of T_xM and B the second fundamental form of N (Ch. 2, 5.9; Ch. 4, 2.7). Hence δV(X) = −∫ X·H dμ_V with H := H_N on M ∩ N and 0 elsewhere (Borel). On a compact K ⊂ U, K ∩ N is compact (N ∩ U relatively closed), B is continuous, so |H| ≤ √n·sup_{K∩N}|B| μ_V-a.e. on K. This is HasLocallyBoundedMeanCurvature. (If ℓ = k, B = 0 and H = 0.)
proof_key_steps: n = 0 gives T = 0; otherwise H^n(M∖N) = 0 and flows of fields tangent to N preserve N ∩ U.
φ_{t#}T are integer multiplicity competitors, so the first variation of their mass vanishes: stationarity in N ∩ U.
Splitting X into tangential and normal parts gives δV(X) = −∫X·H_N dμ_V with H_N locally bounded.
